FORMAL-SYSTEM · qeva:1:formal-system@1

Formal system

A declared language together with axioms and inference rules used to determine which expressions count as derivable.

editoriallogic · foundations

PLAIN

The idea

A formal system fixes the symbols you may write, the starting statements you accept, and the rules by which new statements may be derived.

EXACT

The compact statement

For QEVA seed purposes, a formal system S is specified by at least a formal language L, a designated set or scheme of axioms A, and inference rules R. A complete record must also state any syntax and proof conventions required to determine valid derivations.

EXAMPLE

A presentation of propositional logic may specify formulas, axiom schemes, and modus ponens.

BOUNDARY / CAVEAT

Different foundations package syntax, axioms, rules, semantics, and definitions differently; QEVA must record the chosen presentation rather than force one universal encoding.

ASSUMPTIONS

  • No assumptions declared.

PROVENANCE

Seed record written to make QEVA Protocol 0.2 explicit. It is an editorial mathematical formulation, not a claim that one foundation is uniquely privileged.
